answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with slashable stake plus a watermark: each identity must lock a bond and carry a credential whose pigment is a unique nonce baked into its signature, so peers can spot clones. Trust builds slowly along a ridge of verified past jobs, meaning a brand-new name starts with no weight. If many aliases echo the same nonce, all of their bonds are slashed together. To fake a thousand workers an attacker must lock a thousand separate stakes, so the cost of the sybil campaign exceeds any reward the fraud could steal.
